title: Depression and Anxiety
author: William Saville
content:
Having depression is hard,
Having anxiety is hard,
Having both is a nightmare.
Anxiety is like drowning in a series of plans and canceled outings and
hanging on for dear life to SOMETHING.
Depression is drowning in your own thoughts, fears, and having no energy
to even breathe.
Breathing.
It used to be easy,
But now it makes me queezy.
I try to stay afloat,
But my body just likes sinking.
My coping mechanisms are self harming,
And my thoughts are alarming.
And I don't know how to stop them.
Anxiety is not being able to catch your breath.
So when you have no energy to breathe,
And you can't catch your breath.
Your mind fills with thoughts of death.
How easy would it be?
Depression is wanting to give in.
Anxiety is thinking of everything LEFT for you to do.
The people you will disappoint.
The people you will hurt.
Depression tells you that they won't miss you,
They are better without you.
Anxiety tells you they care too much what they think of you.
Anxiety and depression battle in my mind.
Depression makes me not want to get up to shower,
Anxiety makes me shake with fear,
That my body will disgust those around me.
So I shower anyways.
And while I am under the scalding hot water,
Desperate to wash the sweat and fear off of my skin,
I think that my depression will win,
While I am under the water I think,
"Electrocution isn't so bad"
But then my anxiety tells me,
No one wants to see your DISGUSTING naked body.
So I stay alive.
Too tired to continue,
Too scared to end it.
I hold on to little experiences that make me happy,
But so much is pretend,
So much is forced.
So much is coerced.
Genuine human connection scares me.
But I can't live without it.
So I just keep treading water.
Face inches from the surface.
Surviving in a world,
That I never thought I would grow up to see.
A world I never prepared for.
I never thought I would live to 18, let alone 24.
And it shakes me to the core.
When you spend your life just surviving.
You don't learn how to live.
